This Interpretative Note provides a structured and operational representation of the data points set out under the draft Implementing Technical Standard (ITS) under Article 69(3) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1624(AMLR). It proposes technical specifications for each data point as a convergence objective among Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs), as well as practical guidance and details for filling out the templates.
The Note is published by AMLA with the purpose of:
- facilitating the reporting process
- guiding the technical implementation into FIUs’ and obliged entities reporting systems
- promoting data standardisation and harmonisation, and
- enhancing data quality and exchanges.
The clarifications set out in this Note are technical in nature and are provided solely for facilitating the implementation and the reporting of the datapoints required under the relevant draft ITS.
Reporting obliged entities are expected to adhere to these explanations to ensure consistency of the data reported.

This Note does not create, amend or supersede any legally binding requirement and does not provide legal assurance. In the event of any inconsistency, the applicable Union legal acts (including Regulations and delegated/implementing acts, such as RTS/ITS) shall prevail. Scope of the Note and future updates This Interpretative Note supports only the reporting of suspicions and the provision of transaction records as required by FIUs under EU and national applicable laws, whose format is developed in the draft ITS pursuant to Article 69(3) AMLR.

Future updates will be developed under a collective and structured process involving FIUs and coordinated by AMLA under the decision of the General Board of AMLA or a representative body chosen by it.
Where helpful, the Interpretative Note includes:
- High-level attributes (free text, enumeration, numeric value, etc.)

- Guide for reporting the data points or using the various categories As a general guidance, data points need to be filled in accordance with the sector and the products and services provided by the reporting entity. This means that not all templates will be applicable to every reporting obliged entity.

Section 1: reports of suspicions Data points are organised in various categories which should be reported depending on the type of activity carried out by the reporting obliged entity and the type of suspicion reported. The dependencies between data points and the relations with the type of obliged entity are described in the annexes of the draft ITS pursuant to Article 69(3) AMLR.

Depending on some of the answers provided to some data points, some categories or data points will not be requested to the reporting obliged entity. Among those visible, only the ones referred to as “mandatory” must be filled. The ones referred to as “mandatory if available” must be filled only where the information is available (e.g.: the previous identity of a natural person is not requested if it is unknown or does not exist). The ones referred to as “optional” must be reported where they are considered relevant and proportionate by the obliged entity.

1.1 “Report” category This category captures the relevant general information related to the report. Some of the data points support the selection of other data points or categories depending on the activity of the reporting obliged entity and the suspicion reported.

1.11 Links The general approach of the datamodel is to provide flexible framework to represent various relations that can arise between individual categories of the template, while still keeping the basic logic of the relations among the categories intact. Below is a matrix of all categories that constitute the template and the relationships arising therefrom. Combinations which are not sensible from the perspective of reporting shall be omitted. The category of a linkage is determined by each of its constituent categories for each constituent category - e.g. R-NP denotes links between Report (R) and Natural Person (NP). Links do not connect particular datapoint (such as account number) but the entities as a whole - for the purposes of links, an instance of, for example, account is comprised of all the datapoints which constitute that category. Linkage connects the abstract concept of an account (in terms of XSD it would be expressed as complex element) to another abstract concept such as the person - the values of a link then represent various relationships which are possible between the linked categories. In addition to that, links may also include other datapoints, for example on relationship start and termination dates. These datapoints will be denoted with the "Relationship Details" category. There can be multiple linkages between the same individual objects (e.g. a person can be shareholder, CEO and UBO of a company).
